outputData.altText: புல்வெளியில் நிற்கும் கறுப்புக் குதிரை மற்றும் அதன் மேலே பறக்கும் ஒரு பறவை.
outputData.detailedDescription: இந்தப் படம் ஒரு கருப்பு மற்றும் வெள்ளை (Monochrome) புகைப்படமாகும். இதில் ஒரு பெரிய கறுப்பு நிறக் குதிரை உயரமான புல்வெளியின் நடுவில் கம்பீரமாக நிற்கிறது. குதிரையின் தலை சற்று வலதுபுறமாகத் திரும்பி உள்ளது, அதன் கருமையான தலைமுடியும் பிடறியும் காற்றில் பறக்கின்றன. குதிரையின் உடல் வாகு மிகவும் வலுவாகவும் நேர்த்தியாகவும் உள்ளது. குதிரைக்கு சற்று மேலே, இடது பக்கத்தில் ஒரு பறவை வானத்தில் பறந்து கொண்டிருக்கிறது. பின்னணியில் மூடிய மேகங்களுடன் கூடிய சாம்பல் நிற வானம் மற்றும் பரந்த புல்வெளி காணப்படுகிறது. ஒட்டுமொத்தப் படமும் ஒரு அமைதியான, அதே சமயம் கம்பீரமான உணர்வைத் தருகிறது.

outputData.altText: புல்வெளியில் நிற்கும் கரிய குதிரையும், மேலே பறக்கும் பறவையும் கொண்ட கருப்பு வெள்ளை படம்.

outputData.title: The Complete Hostel Balanced Diet Chart (With Night Milk)
outputData.summary:
This diet chart provides a balanced meal plan for hostel students, structured across seven days of the week. Each day is organized into four main meal categories with specific nutritional focuses:

*   **Morning Breakfast (Probiotics & Protein):** Typically includes Fermented Rice and Shop Curd, often costing around ₹12.
*   **Afternoon Lunch (Carbs & Fats):** Consists of standard Mess Meals, Buttermilk, and a handful of Peanuts, with an approximate cost of ₹20.
*   **Evening Snack (Plant Protein):** A consistent offering of a handful of Pottukadalai is provided daily.
*   **Night Dinner & Bedtime (Recovery & Growth):** Dinners vary each night, featuring options such as Gobi Rice, Soya Fried Rice, Chicken Night, Rice & Sambar, and Soya Chunks Biryani. Most dinners include 2 Kettle-Boiled Eggs or a Mess Egg, and a Banana is included on Monday.
*   **Night Milk** is a crucial and consistent component consumed every night to aid in recovery and growth.
*   **Sunday's schedule** offers some flexibility, allowing for sleeping in or a light mess breakfast, and a 'Rest' option for the evening snack if the student is full.

Use an electric kettle in your room to boil eggs or cook soya chunks to add to your dinner.
Get fresh milk daily to drink before going to sleep.

inputData.transcriptSnippet: Today we discuss sound waves. Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave that travels through matter by compressing and decompressing particles.

outputData.title: Introduction to Sound Waves
outputData.summary:
This lecture introduces the basic properties of sound waves:
*   Sound is a specific type of wave known as a "longitudinal mechanical wave."
*   As a mechanical wave, sound requires a medium (matter) to travel through; it cannot travel in a vacuum.
*   Sound travels through matter by causing particles to move closer together (compressing) and then spread apart (decompressing).

keyTerms.explanation: A type of wave where the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth in the same direction that the wave is traveling.
A wave that requires a medium (matter) to travel through. It cannot travel in empty space.
The action of pushing particles in a material closer together, increasing their density.
The action of allowing particles in a material to spread further apart, decreasing their density.

quiz.question: According to the lecture, what type of wave is sound?
quiz.explanation: The lecture explicitly states, 'Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave.'

quiz.question: How does sound travel through matter?
options: C. By compressing and decompressing particles
quiz.correctAnswer: C. By compressing and decompressing particles
quiz.explanation: The lecture explains that sound 'travels through matter by compressing and decompressing particles.'

quiz.question: What does it mean for sound to be a 'mechanical wave'?
options: A. It can travel through empty space.
B. It requires a medium (matter) to travel.
C. It is powered by machines.
D. It only travels in one direction.
quiz.correctAnswer: B. It requires a medium (matter) to travel.
quiz.explanation: A mechanical wave, like sound, needs matter (a medium) to move through. The lecture states it 'travels through matter.'

• Light particles (photons) hit the silicon cell.
• This knocks electrons loose, creating an electric current.
• The resulting direct current (DC) is then converted for home use.

keyTerms.explanation: The process of turning light particles directly into electricity.
A tiny particle of light carrying radiant energy.
The boundary inside a semiconductor that guides electrical current in one direction.
